newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi shares rise on Smithkline Beecham bonus.
newsitem.headline: Delhi shares rise on Smithkline Beecham bonus.

text.p: Heavy buying in Smithkline Beecham Consumer Healthcare Ltd triggered by its announcement of a bonus share issue pushed Delhi shares higher in early trade on Wednesday, brokers said.
The Delhi Stock Exchange's sensitive index was 2.01 points higher at 790.44 after 30 minutes of trade.
Smithkline Beecham, which on Tuesday offered a bonus of three shares for every five shares held, shot up 20 rupees, or 6.7 percent, to 320, brokers said.
"The announcement of the bonus was totally unexpected as the company had already rewarded the shareholders with a one-for-one issue in 1995," said S.C. Juneja of brokers Jaico Credit.

Smithkline Beecham said after-tax profit jumped 30 percent to 469.4 million rupees for the financial year ended on December 31. Profit before tax was 793.1 million rupees, it said without giving a comparative figure for 1995.
Brokers said start of a new settlement period at the National Stock Exchange also pushed up share prices as speculators created fresh positions.
"The start of new settlement on the National Stock Exchange also generated buying among local speculators to some extent," said Sanjay Mittal of brokers S.R.M. Securities.
State Bank of India gained 2.00 rupees to 322.55.
